rationale: Open an independent, source-only question on the authority-transition side of configuration changes. The plausible hazard is that the pending-change gate counts only entries after the committed index and is a single boolean cleared by any applied change, so a leader that inherits a committed but unapplied configuration change could accept a second change and commit it with the pre-change membership. The turn traces the proposal gate, the leadership-recovery check and the election gate to decide whether that history is permitted, and records the result as a refuted suspicion with its residual liveness tradeoff rather than as a defect.

investigations.question: After a leadership change, can a leader accept and commit a configuration change while an inherited configuration change is committed but not yet applied, so the newer change is committed with the pre-change quorum?
investigations.hypothesis: The pending-change gate counts only entries after the committed index and is a single boolean cleared by any applied change, so a leader that inherits a committed-but-unapplied configuration change could accept a second change and commit it with the membership that still excludes the first change.

knowledge.statement: handleLeaderPropose inspects every proposed entry, reports a configuration-change entry as dropped and replaces it with an empty application entry when pendingConfigChange is already set, and sets that flag for each configuration-change entry it inspects before appending the remaining entries and replicating them. The apply paths addNode, addObserver, addWitness and removeNode clear the flag, and reset clears it on a term or role transition, so a leader that proposed a configuration change keeps refusing new configuration changes until a configuration change is applied or the peer changes term or role.
knowledge.conditions: The peer is leader, configuration-change proposals arrive through handleLeaderPropose, and configuration changes are applied through the raft apply paths and reported by the surrounding node.

knowledge.statement: handleNodeElection refuses to campaign when log.committed exceeds the applied index, using the general committed-versus-applied check rather than a configuration-specific one, so a node with any committed but unapplied entry cannot start an election. preLeaderPromotionHandleConfigChange then counts only configuration-change entries after the committed index and re-sets the pending flag when exactly one exists, or panics when more than one exists. handleFollowerTimeoutNow reaches the same election handler because it only advances the election tick and lets the normal tick emit the Election message, and tryCommit evaluates the cluster quorum from the raft membership maps that the apply paths maintain.
knowledge.conditions: Elections start through the Election message, including the path taken after a leader-transfer TimeoutNow, and the applied index is the value the surrounding node reports after its state machine applies entries.

interpretations.rationale: The suspicion is refuted for the captured raft paths. The hazard requires a leader whose log holds a committed configuration change that its membership maps have not yet applied, because tryCommit computes the quorum from those maps and a second change committed before the first is applied would be committed with the pre-change quorum. Two gates prevent that history. A leader that proposed a configuration change sets pendingConfigChange in handleLeaderPropose and keeps it set until a configuration-change apply path clears it, so any further configuration change it proposes is reported dropped and replaced with an empty application entry; the leader cannot accumulate a second uncommitted change while the first is committed but unapplied. A node that did not propose the change can only become leader by campaigning, and handleNodeElection refuses to campaign while log.committed exceeds the applied index, so a node that still has any committed unapplied entry, including a configuration change, cannot become leader; TimeoutNow cannot bypass this because it only advances the election tick and lets the normal tick emit the Election message that handleNodeElection gates. preLeaderPromotionHandleConfigChange therefore runs only after the applied index has caught up with the committed index, and its count of entries after the committed index is consistent with that state; it re-sets the pending flag for the single uncommitted change it can legitimately find and panics if the log ever holds more than one. The consequence is an availability tradeoff rather than the suspected safety violation: while the applied index lags, the node declines to campaign, and a leader keeps dropping configuration changes until the in-flight change is applied. The low-level pieces that suggested the hazard remain exactly as described, but the permitted leadership and proposal histories do not produce the required state.
counterevidence: getPendingConfigChangeCount starts at the committed index plus one, so a committed but unapplied configuration change is never counted as pending, and pendingConfigChange is a single boolean that does not record which change it tracks.

tryCommit computes the quorum from the raft membership maps, which the apply paths change only when a configuration change is applied, so the hazard would be real if a leader could accept a second change before the first was applied.

The election gate is a general committed-versus-applied comparison, so the refutation depends on the applied index being advanced only after the state machine has applied those entries, which is the value node.updateAppliedIndex forwards.
limitations: This is a source-only account; no execution of the leadership, proposal or apply ordering is retained for it.

Direct mutation of the internal role maps, an operator starting a node with a role inconsistent with cluster membership, forged messages, and a custom transport that changes message admission are excluded.
The gate is a liveness tradeoff: a node whose applied index lags cannot campaign and a leader keeps dropping configuration changes, and no bound on that delay is established.
Snapshot restore and configuration changes carried by snapshots are covered only by the role guards recorded elsewhere, not by this account.
